value: buckwheat grown under LED light in a phytotron chamber was more compact (smaller leaf area) and had lower main stem height than plants in a glasshouse under solar light supplemented with HPS lamps; the comparison bundles light with production system
method: experimental light contrast, bundled with growth system: 10 pots of 5 plants per treatment, LED-only phytotron chamber against glasshouse solar light plus HPS lamps; biometrics n = 10 per treatment
conditions: single cultivar 'Panda', 10 pots of five plants per treatment, eight weeks in August and September 2020; both systems 16 h photoperiod and the same stated temperature (25/22 C day/night) and humidity (55 to 60 percent) setpoints, with no separate measured values given; LED average about 300 umol m-2 s-1, a 200 W full-spectrum LED (380 to 840 nm; the red and blue shares are given only in the Discussion); glasshouse sunlight up to 1300 to 1600 umol m-2 s-1 on a cloudless day plus 300 umol m-2 s-1 from HPS; CO2 not reported; treatment is chamber against glasshouse, so light (intensity, spectrum, daily dose) is not isolated from other system differences. Table 1 (means, n = 10, +/- SE, Student's t test) marks main stem height as significantly lower under LED (p < 0.01) and the area of the third leaf (the only leaf area measured) as lower (p < 0.001), but shows no significant difference in the number of main stem internodes, so the quote's 'more internodes' is not a significant result; the Table 1 means are not quoted here. The HPS hours differ within the paper: Methods 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., the DLI sentence 'supplemented for 4 h', the Fig. 3 caption 6.00 to 10.00 a.m. Same paper: phenolics and flavonoids higher under LED, fresh and dry weight lower

source.title: Photosynthetic efficiency, growth and secondary metabolism of common buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum Moench) in different controlled-environment production systems

quote: Common buckwheat plants grown under LED light were more compact (smaller leaf area and more internodes) and showed lower main stem height than the plants grown in the glasshouse with solar light supplemented with HPS lamps (Table 1).
note: Growth endpoint under a bundled lighting and production-system contrast, not an isolated light effect; filed under sense_light_nonvisual as an experimental light contrast with the bundle stated (LIGHT-RESPONSE.md: confounded chamber/site treatment is eligible with bundle and limits identified); evidence_kind physiological_response.
